A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new adversarial attacking method that exploits the class-wise and layerwise feature distribution of deep neural network (DNN) models to generate transferable adversarial examples, and further we provide a novel perspective on the feature distributional properties of DNN models.
the proposed method is able to generate adversarial images which can fool a target network with a higher success rate than previous methods.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the transferability of deep adversarial examples is not only due to model similarity, but also to the distributional similarity of deep features across models.
a better understanding of deep feature distributions and how they evolve within a CNN architecture is key to improving the transferability of blackbox adversarial attacks.
